title: Middle of Linked List
contract: Return the second middle value for an even-length nonempty list.
brute: Node head=list(input);int size=0;for(Node n=head;n!=null;n=n.next)size++;Node node=head;for(int i=0;i<size/2;i++){node=node.next;emit("Walk to the counted middle","index",i+1);}return node.value;
optimal: Node slow=list(input),fast=slow;while(fast!=null&&fast.next!=null){slow=slow.next;fast=fast.next.next;emit("Fast moves twice as far","slow value",slow.value,"fast value",fast==null?null:fast.value);}return slow.value;
reasoning: Count nodes, then walk halfway in a second traversal.
When fast has moved 2k links, slow has moved k links. Exhausting fast places slow at the second middle.
Both approaches are linear and constant auxiliary space; the improvement is a single traversal. List construction from the demo array is excluded from traversal-space analysis.
complexity: O(n), O(1) traversal space; one pass
